title: Flow Cytometry for Monocyte Phenotype and Mitochondrial Mass
author: Brandt D Pence
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kw8cxhw
materials: Add antibodies to tubes:CD14 antibody: 20 μl to all samples plus CD14 only control, FMO no CD16, FMO no MitotrackerCD16 antibody: 1 μl to all samples plus CD16 only control, FMO no CD14, FMO no Mitotracker

Data Analysis For the listed antibodies, a flow cytometer with blue (488 nm) and violet (405 nm) lasers is necessary. Adjust forward scatter, side scatter, and fluorescence detector sensitivity as appropriate. Gate based on unstained control and FMO controls with compensation based on single stain tubes. Gate monocyte population ( Figure 1A ) and show scatter plot of CD16 vs. CD14 ( Figure 1B ). Mitotracker data can be analyzed as median fluorescence intensity between samples or cell populations. a Figure 1. Typical flow cytometry results. (A) Typical forward and side scatter plot. Monocytes are gated. (B) Typical CD16 vs. CD14 plot. Monocytes are separated into classical (CD14+CD16-), intermediate (CD14+CD16+), and non-classical (CD14dimCD16+) subtypes.
Materials to Prepare Mitotracker Green FM Prepare as directed and store 1mM stock solution at -20 o C.

steps.title: Collect blood in K2EDTA
steps.instruction: Collect blood in a K2EDTA tube and store the tube at room temperature until use.

steps.title: Aliquot whole blood into tubes
steps.instruction: Aliquot 100 μL of whole blood into each 12 × 75 mm test tube, using one tube per subject.

steps.title: Prepare control tubes
steps.instruction: Aliquot 100 μL of blood into separate control tubes (using blood from one subject or a mixed pool). Prepare the following controls: (a) Unstained control, (b) CD14‑only control, (c) CD16‑only control, (d) Mitotracker‑only control, (e) FMO no CD14, (f) FMO no CD16, (g) FMO no Mitotracker. FMO (fluorescence‑minus‑one) includes all stains except the one indicated.

steps.title: Add IgG and block Fc receptors
steps.instruction: Add 10 μg IgG to each tube and incubate for 15 minutes at 4 °C–25 °C to block Fc receptors.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Vortex gently and incubate the tubes for 1 hour in the dark at 4 °C–25 °C.

steps.title: Lyse cells with buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of lysing buffer to each tube, vortex gently, and incubate in the dark at 4 °C–25 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Mitotracker staining solution
steps.instruction: While lysing, prepare Mitotracker solution: dilute 1 μL of stock into 999 μL stain buffer, then take 200 μL of this dilution and add 800 μL stain buffer to obtain a final concentration of 200 nM.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysed blood at 500 × g for 5 minutes, then carefully remove and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Add Mitotracker or buffer to tubes
steps.instruction: Add 200 μL Mitotracker to all samples plus the Mitotracker‑only control, FMO no CD14, and FMO no CD16 tubes. Add 200 μL staining buffer to the unstained control, CD14‑only, CD16‑only, and FMO no Mitotracker tubes.

steps.title: Incubate staining reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes for 1 hour in the dark at 4 °C–25 °C.

steps.title: Wash cells with staining buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL staining buffer to each tube, centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes, and remove the supernatant. Repeat the addition of 1 mL staining buffer, centrifugation, and supernatant removal for a second wash.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL staining buffer, centrifuge 500 × g 5 min, discard supernatant.
Repeat: add 1 mL staining buffer, centrifuge 500 × g 5 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend and acquire data
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 400 μL lysing buffer and analyze the samples by flow cytometry as quickly as possible.
